Joe Rogan turns to the overuse of Monsanto's Roundup weedkiller and the super weeds it bred in a segment from his show. Roundup is sprayed on farms and lawns in vast amounts. Weeds that shrug it off now plague fields.

Rogan works through how the spray arms race played out, as growers poured on more to kill tougher weeds. He asks what the flood of spray means for food, soil, and health. The segment is short and sharp. Listeners get a brisk take on a farm crisis with wide reach. The library holds the file as an archive record.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. joins Tucker Carlson to talk about the murder of his uncle, President John F. Kennedy. Kennedy was shot in Dallas in 1963, and the official story has been doubted ever since. Few guests can speak about that day as family, and that shapes the whole talk.

Kennedy shares what he believes about who was involved and why the full truth stayed hidden. He points at intelligence agencies and at years of sealed records and shifting stories. Carlson asks how the killing changed his own family and the country. The result is a personal take on one of America's most argued-over events.
